result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Repository-wide static assessment of security configuration, controllers/service logs, runtime properties, Docker/Compose, Oracle scripts, Azure scripts, MCP environment references, workflow credential references, README and environment examples. Production passwords are supplied through environment variables or generated with a cryptographic RNG; no production hard-coded password or cryptographic key was confirmed. Test-only credentials and example placeholders are excluded as vulnerability evidence and their values are omitted. Azure secret-file effective permissions depend on inherited ACL/umask; absence of explicit permission-setting alone was not asserted as confirmed overbroad access. No application source changes or tests performed.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging

evidence.explanation: SecurityConfig.securityFilterChain lines 54-60 requires HTTP Basic authentication for uploads and deletions. Nevertheless DetailController.deletePhoto lines 64-76 logs only the photo ID and outcome; PhotoServiceImpl.deletePhoto lines 199-216 and uploadPhoto lines 173-184 likewise log object IDs/filenames without the authenticated principal, source client or audit correlation. These are security-critical mutation events, but the application logs omit attribution to the actor. This finding is insufficient audit detail, not a claim that mutations have no logging or that Spring Security never emits any diagnostic logs. The supplied in-memory user store currently contains one admin account; the logs still cannot distinguish the client responsible for an operation.

values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
